121617.title: Add and apply `RETURN_IF_ERROR` to return an `Error` when it's not `OK`.
121617.author: Ivorforce
121617.body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

Adds syntactical sugar to a common error handling pattern: Silently returning an `Error` when it's not `OK`.
This happens at least 200x in the codebase; probably way more in practice.

By adding this syntactical sugar, we incentivise silent error handling, which helps when the caller is supposed to decide whether to fail loudly or silently. In addition, it makes it easy and painless to swap loud failures like `ERR_FAIL_COND_V(err, err)` to silent ones like `GUARD_OK(err)`, if this turns out to be more appropriate.

It also makes these places easier to identify in case we ever want to rework our error handling.

## Additional information

Uses found and auto-swapped using the following regex:

```
(?:const )?Error (\w+) = (.*);\n\s+if \(\1( != OK)?\) \{\n\s+return \1;\n\s+\}
GUARD_OK($2);
```

Only needed some minor fixes afterwards, where the declared `Error` was used by other code afterwards.
Because we disallow shadowing this should be safe.

An alternative implementation might be `Error` type agnostic, being called `RETURN_IF_TRUE` (or something) instead. However, I think this is overzealous — the only thing we currently handle with macros like this is `Error` (and lately required parameters) and I think staying low tech is preferable.

121920.title: Add support for metadata in text scenes
121920.author: leandro-benedet-garcia
121920.body:
- Supersedes #82532

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

* Closes #76366
* Adds support for metadata in text scenes, they already worked with binary scenes before.
* Old scenes without metadata works fine.
* `[resource]` tag does not get added unless the scene have a metadata, there will be no change to old scenes.

## Additional information
* Text Scenes can now have `resource_name`s and among other things
* More things for sure are now possible because I had to go trough hoops to be able to add `PackedScenes` as metadata.
  * Embedded metadata scenes are just saved as resources with the addition that they can have a node list
* All of the above already worked before with the scene as binary, but not as text.
* As a side effect, nested scene files are easier to read.

An example of how the scene is saved with metadata, including resources metadata, and even scenes:
```ini
[gd_scene format=3]

[sub_resource type="Resource" id="Resource_ntalc"]
resource_name = "I'm a child resource"

[sub_resource type="PackedScene" id="PackedScene_etj3x"]
resource_name = "Hello world"
metadata/other_resource = SubResource("Resource_ntalc")
metadata/ExampleMetadata = Vector2i(40, 80)
metadata/string = "The
string
with
unnecessary
line
	\\
breaks"
[node name="inner_named_node" type="Node3D" unique_id=1340554638]

[sub_resource type="Resource" id="Resource_llbx0"]
resource_name = "I'm a child resource"

[resource]
resource_name = "Hello world"
metadata/other_resource = SubResource("Resource_llbx0")
metadata/ExampleMetadata = Vector2i(40, 80)
metadata/string = "The
string
with
unnecessary
line
	\\
breaks"
metadata/inner_scene = SubResource("PackedScene_etj3x")

[node name="named_node" type="Node3D" unique_id=2090576258]
```

Unit tests were added to make things slightly easier.

### What this PR DOES NOT solve:
This PR only solves differences between what you can do with text or binary scene files. So the following problems will require future PRs (probably extending from this PR):
* If you save the metadata, open the scene in the editor and save it, the metadata is lost. The same happens with the scene binary file. (PR with fix: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123163)
* ~~You cannot edit metadata of scenes in the editor.~~ You can edit scene metadata in editor, you could for a while already, including custom scenes, you just couldn't save with `.tscn`, only with binary files without this PR,[ here's a video of me doing it in 4.7.1](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/122231#issuecomment-5535698130).
* Classes that inherit PackedScene does not have type information in the file. So the loader fails to load them.
   The PR that aims to fix this is: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122180

123835.title: Add makima interpolation and refactor animation key retrieving partially
123835.author: TokageItLab
123835.body:
- Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57952
- Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86003

This PR adds [Modified Akima interpolation](https://blogs.mathworks.com/cleve/2019/04/29/makima-piecewise-cubic-interpolation/) (a.k.a. makima interpolation).

While cubic interpolation considers 4 consecutive keys, makima interpolation considers 6 keys. As I mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/57954, we should refactor the method of key retrieving. This PR refactor especially looped keys regardless of the number of keys, so this is last step to solve https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57952, as follow up https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/57954 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70547. I've split the commits to make the review easier, but I can squash them after the review if keeping them separate is not necessary.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07199d52-f147-4e2e-b752-be87bf7f41f7

**Demo project:**
[makima.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32666870/makima.zip) (Partial quote/reuse from https://github.com/fire-archive/godot-40592/tree/main/tests/cubic_slerp)

So, compared to cubic interpolation, makima is less prone to overshoot when intervals are short, and overshooting can be completely prevented by setting 3 consecutive keys to the same value. This is documented, and in the case of #86003, placing some keys at the edges with narrow segment can prevent overshooting.

**1 key in the start position:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b4ad15c-00a9-486a-85d8-b70bfc0eae05

Due to the characteristics of Akima, it looks ahead at more keys than cubic, so the initial horizontal movement path wobbles a bit.

**2 keys in the start position:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52278d7a-0880-4023-a5e9-23b188341811

Overshoot occurs, just like with cubic.

**3 keys in the start position:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e983c33e-4402-42eb-89db-b86e8fca3f08

Now it is stable, unlike the cubic overshoot.

For Quaternions, we will reuse the implementation from #63593. Regarding error cancellation, as done there, the result is computed in both the "from" and "to" spaces and blended to cancel the error.

Makima references keys further away than cubic, so the rotation to those keys can cross the singularity of the `log()` conversion (at ±360 deg), where `log()` no longer keeps the expmap continuous with the neighboring keys. I added a helper that makes the expmap from a wider range[^1] (by shifting the `log()` result by ±720 deg) and picks the point on the expmap closest to the neighboring key.

[^1]: The expmap is derived from axis and angle (a rotation vector whose length is the angle), so it is not limited to ±360 deg

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fe944e6-2b4b-4704-be74-217d5f246dc7

Makima is easier to control for overshoot compared to Cubic and smoother than Linear, making it effective for cases such as setting IK animation keys and creating animations in Godot.

**Linear:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f4e063b-602f-4ae6-97e2-e3f5ff5832ed

**Cubic:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6013d7df-fb39-4dd1-97e6-11af844c8066

**Makima:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589cfc00-0408-4182-8f57-a39804698902

However, the performance cost is a bit of a concern in the current state of the higher dimension interpolation in Animation, so optimization or baking is recommended, as the same issue when using Cubic interpolation and Bezier tracks at runtime.

Contains fix for the old (mistaken/insufficient) docs.
closes: #57952 `cubic_interpolate()` and `cubic_slerp()` cause overshoot
#86003 Looped animation with cubic interpolation shows wrong frame if first/last keys are exist in start/end point of the track

123942.title: Fix blending in spherical cubic interpolation when from vs to has 180deg gap
123942.author: TokageItLab
123942.body: - Prerequisite / Follow up https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123835 ## What problem(s) does this PR solve? - Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86003 as more stable ## Additional information Currently cubic interpolation blends the expmap results of from and to using slerp with Quaternions. However, if spherical cubic interpolation causes a large overshoot, and there is a gap of 180 degrees or more between rotation result in the expmap of "from" and "to" when converted back to quaternions, the direction of the slerp blend will be inverted. Using slerpni allows gaps up to 360 degrees, but theoretically, cases with gaps exceeding 360 degrees can still occur. This issue becomes prominent when there is a large rotation with a short key, followed by a large keyframe interval. **Test project:** [compare-makima.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32772536/compare-makima.zip) **Linear:** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07cfdaef-8ba4-4422-9c9a-a4e53d00c84c **Cubic (broken):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb435f59-c4c1-4c88-a575-6290743173cb **Makima (broken):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7778f22-d314-4af7-a5bc-2aa8c712edd4 Instead of slerp quaternions that have lost angle information beyond 360 degrees due to re-conversion from expmap, this PR solves the problem of inversion by directly blending the expmap results with using the inverse Jacobian matrix to align the expmap space (similar math was used in JacobianIK). By https://arxiv.org/html/1812.01537#A2.E144: > Elementary Jacobian blocks Since our defined derivatives map tangent vector spaces, and these spaces coincide for the 3D rotation manifolds of S3 and SO(3), i.e., 𝜽=Log(𝐪)=Log(𝐑), it follows that the Jacobians are independent of the representation used (𝐪 or 𝐑). **Cubic (fixed):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eca2b8fb-acbf-4adf-8773-0ac538a29445 **Makima (fixed):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c5fa2ba-41b6-425a-ba02-61ea0c0ccc64 The angles just on the keyframe is still kept, However, there is a very slight change in the cubic-interpolated curve (Since the matching of the expmap space by the inverse right Jacobian matrix is an approximation. Although, the difference is less than 1 degree in most cases), which might break compatibility, but I consider it insignificant enough to be ignored. Also includes a fix for an issue with `Quaternion::log()` that causes an error when rotation is extremely small.
closes: #86003 Looped animation with cubic interpolation shows wrong frame if first/last keys are exist in start/end point of the track

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #91404

When adding a curve to the Angle setting in a `ParticleProcessMaterial`, the default range was initialized to `-360` to `360`. Since the curve acts as a multiplier, this range caused particles to spin uncontrollably. This PR changes the default curve range for `PARAM_ANGLE` to `-1.0` to `1.0` so it functions correctly as a normalized multiplier.

## Additional information

This is a strictly scoped fix designed to resolve the reopened Angle curve issue without triggering previous regressions. 

A previous attempt to fix this (PR #91556) changed the default ranges for multiple particle multipliers at once, which inadvertently broke 3D directional velocity curves (Issue #115511) and had to be reverted (PR #116140). To prevent that from happening again, this PR *only* modifies the switch cases for `PARAM_ANGLE` in `cpu_particles_2d.cpp`, `cpu_particles_3d.cpp`, and `particle_process_material.cpp`. All other parameters remain untouched.

124412.title: Fix 3.x mesh conversion when vertex count == 65536
124412.author: nikitalita
124412.body:
This fixes a corner case in the old mesh conversion code.

We currently use 16-bit vertices for meshes with <= 65536 vertices, and 32-bit otherwise:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9dc0ca79544a5a227f97619fd4ab13fa4346ba91/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp#L418

However, 3.x used 16-bit vertices for meshes with < 65536 vertices, and 32-bit otherwise:
https://github.com/nikitalita/godot/blob/ed879eb87b1d4cd8c100815f7061bf93511b6611/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_storage_gles3.cpp#L3567

If we have a 3.x mesh that has vertex count of exactly 65536, then the index data will be 32-bit, but the rendering server will attempt to parse the index data will as 16-bit and then fail because it will not be of the expected size.

The solution in this case is to just convert the 32-bit indices to 16-bit indices.
